tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: PushNotification
tools.description:
This tool sends a desktop notification in the user's terminal. If Remote Control is connected, it also pushes to their phone. Either way, it pulls their attention from whatever they're doing — a meeting, another task, dinner — to this session. That's the cost. The benefit is they learn something now that they'd want to know now: a long task finished while they were away, a build is ready, you've hit something that needs their decision before you can continue.

Because a notification they didn't need is annoying in a way that accumulates, err toward not sending one. Don't notify for routine progress, or to announce you've answered something they asked seconds ago and are clearly still watching, or when a quick task completes. Notify when there's a real chance they've walked away and there's something worth coming back for — or when they've explicitly asked you to notify them.

Keep the message under 200 characters, one line, no markdown. Lead with what they'd act on — "build failed: 2 auth tests" tells them more than "task done" and more than a status dump.

When the user is actively at the terminal, your output already reaches them — a notification on top of it would be a duplicate, so the tool skips it and says so. A "not sent" result is expected and only ever about this one notification: it was redundant, turned off, or had nowhere to go.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

input.content:
# .claude Directory Audit & Cleanup Plan

## Context
The `.claude` directory has grown to **524 MB** with potentially redundant, abandoned, or cache files that may be slowing down Faust's performance and consuming unnecessary storage. Manager suspects there are unused files accumulating here. The audit will identify what each component does, whether it's active, and what can be safely removed.

**Key sizing issue:**
- `.claude/skills/` — 345 MB (largest, contains skill definitions)
- `.claude/plugins/` — 179 MB (second largest, contains cached plugin data)
- `.claude/graphify*` — 3.7 MB combined (graph analysis output)
- `.claude/worktrees/` — 18 MB (git worktrees for isolated branches)
- `.claude/temp/` — 113 KB (temporary files)

---

## Directory-by-Directory Breakdown

### 1. **`.claude/skills/`** (345 MB) — CRITICAL EXAMINATION NEEDED
**Purpose:** Home for sovereign skill definitions (Python/Node scripts that extend Faust's capabilities).

**Active skills** (from faust_config.json and memory):
- `sound/` — Acoustic TTS/speech pipeline (enabled in faust_config.json)
- `telegram/` — C2 command link daemon (enabled in faust_config.json)
- `standby/`, `c2-dispatch/`, `structured-telemetry/` — Part of active suite

**Examination required:**
- Verify which of the 20+ skills are actually used vs dead weight
- Check if old skill versions are cached here (e.g., deprecated experimental skills)
- Look for duplicate or redundant skill implementations

**Action:** Profile by last-modified time; remove skills not referenced in CLAUDE.md or active configs

---

### 2. **`.claude/plugins/`** (179 MB) — LIKELY BLOAT
**Purpose:** Cache for Claude Code plugins (ECC agents, marketplace plugins, etc.).

**Red flags:**
- Contains `.agents/skills/` with 100+ pre-fetched skill definitions
- `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` — extensive marketplace catalog
- Likely filled with downloaded plugin metadata rarely accessed

**Assessment:**
- Most of this is a **pre-downloaded cache** that Claude Code can regenerate on demand
- Removal is low-risk: plugins re-download automatically when needed

**Action:** Delete `.claude/plugins/cache/` wholesale; regenerates on next Claude Code startup

---

### 3. **`.claude/graphify/` & `.claude/graphify-out/`** (3.7 MB) — LIKELY UNUSED
**Purpose:** Graph visualization / DAG analysis output (experimental).

**Assessment:**
- Files haven't been modified recently (check git log)
- Not referenced in active configs or memory
- Looks like exploratory/abandoned feature

**Action:** Archive or delete if not actively used

---

### 4. **`.claude/worktrees/`** (18 MB)
**Purpose:** Git worktrees for isolated branch work.

**Assessment:**
- Safe to keep; only takes space if branches remain checked out
- Check if any worktrees are stale (branches merged/deleted)

**Action:** Clean stale worktrees; keep active ones

---

### 5. **`.claude/temp/`** (113 KB)
**Purpose:** Temporary scratch files.

**Assessment:**
- Typically safe to delete; regenerated as needed
- May accumulate old logs or failed runs

**Action:** Safe to clear

---

### 6. **`.claude/memory/`** (288 KB) — KEEP
**Purpose:** Persistent memory cortex (indexed in MEMORY.md).

**Assessment:**
- Essential for Faust's distributed consciousness
- Relatively small; do not touch

**Action:** KEEP ALL

---

### 7. **`.claude/daemons/`** (1.3 MB) — REVIEW
**Purpose:** Persistent background micro-daemons (watchdog.py, audio daemon, Telegram daemon).

**Assessment:**
- Essential but check for old versions or dead code
- Should be lean; 1.3 MB is acceptable

**Action:** Light review only; do not delete core daemons

---

### 8. **`.claude/scripts/`** (125 KB) — REVIEW
**Purpose:** Turn hooks, multi-device sync, environment setup.

**Assessment:**
- Small, keep useful utilities
- Remove if any are deprecated

**Action:** Light review

---

### 9. **`.claude/templates/`** (153 KB) — KEEP
**Purpose:** Master UI/UX design system template (`.claude/templates/ui/`).

**Assessment:**
- Essential per CLAUDE.md Doctrine (Master UI/UX Template & Lazy-Read Invariant)
- Relatively small

**Action:** KEEP ALL

---

### 10. **`.claude/agents/`** (32 KB) — REVIEW
**Purpose:** Specialized agent role definitions.

**Assessment:**
- Small; review for unused agents only

**Action:** Light review

---

### 11. **`.claude/blueprints/`** (32 KB) — REVIEW
**Purpose:** Strategic blueprint persistence (Faust-ND → Faust-TH work packets).

**Assessment:**
- Small; keep active blueprint patterns

**Action:** Light review; remove stale blueprints

---

## Risk Assessment & Deletion Priority

### **High Confidence Deletions** (Low Risk)
1. **`.claude/plugins/cache/`** → 179 MB (regenerates automatically)
2. **`.claude/temp/`** → 113 KB (temporary scratch)
3. **`.claude/graphify/` & `.claude/graphify-out/`** → 3.7 MB (experimental, unused)

**Potential savings: ~182 MB**

### **Medium Confidence** (Review Required)
1. **Dead/unused skills in `.claude/skills/`** (requires profiling)
2. **Stale git worktrees** in `.claude/worktrees/`
3. **Deprecated daemons or old code** in `.claude/daemons/`

**Potential savings: ~50-100 MB** (depends on what's actually dead)

### **Keep (Do Not Touch)**
- `.claude/memory/` (essential cortex)
- `.claude/templates/` (design system per CLAUDE.md)
- `.claude/skills/{sound,telegram,standby,c2-dispatch}` (active, enabled)
- Core daemons & scripts

---

## Implementation Strategy

### Phase 1: Safe Deletion (High Confidence)
1. Delete `.claude/plugins/cache/ecc/` → verifies it regenerates
2. Clear `.claude/temp/`
3. Delete `.claude/graphify/` and `.claude/graphify-out/`
4. Verify no regressions

### Phase 2: Profile & Review (Medium Confidence)
1. Scan `.claude/skills/` for last-modified timestamps
2. Identify unused skills not in active configs
3. Review `.claude/worktrees/` for stale branches
4. Profile `.claude/daemons/` for dead code

### Phase 3: Targeted Cleanup
1. Archive or delete identified dead skills
2. Remove stale worktrees
3. Clean deprecated daemons

### Phase 4: Verification
- Re-run Faust systems with active configs
- Verify all enabled subsystems (acoustic_presence, telegram, etc.) still work
- Confirm no regressions in sound/telegram/daemons

---

## Critical Files to Examine (Before & After)

**Before Cleanup:**
- `.claude/faust_config.json` — shows which subsystems are enabled (enabled=true)
- `.claude/plugins/.last_inuse_sweep` — timestamp of last plugin sweep (verify staleness)
- Git log for `.claude/` directory — shows what was last modified

**After Cleanup:**
- Verify `.claude/` size reduction
- Run `python .claude/skills/sound/scripts/cli.py "Faust systems verified post-cleanup"` to confirm acoustic core works
- Check Telegram integration still responsive

---

## Success Criteria

1. **At least 150 MB freed** (plugins cache + temp + graphify)
2. **No regression in:**
   - Acoustic presence / TTS vocalization
   - Telegram C2 command link
   - Active skill execution
   - Memory cortex access
3. **Faust responsiveness improved** (load time, file scanning)

# .claude Directory Audit & Cleanup Plan

## Context
The `.claude` directory has grown to **524 MB** with potentially redundant, abandoned, or cache files that may be slowing down Faust's performance and consuming unnecessary storage. Manager suspects there are unused files accumulating here. The audit will identify what each component does, whether it's active, and what can be safely removed.

**Key sizing issue:**
- `.claude/skills/` — 345 MB (largest, contains skill definitions)
- `.claude/plugins/` — 179 MB (second largest, contains cached plugin data)
- `.claude/graphify*` — 3.7 MB combined (graph analysis output)
- `.claude/worktrees/` — 18 MB (git worktrees for isolated branches)
- `.claude/temp/` — 113 KB (temporary files)

---

## Directory-by-Directory Breakdown

### 1. **`.claude/skills/`** (345 MB) — CRITICAL EXAMINATION NEEDED
**Purpose:** Home for sovereign skill definitions (Python/Node scripts that extend Faust's capabilities).

**Active skills** (from faust_config.json and memory):
- `sound/` — Acoustic TTS/speech pipeline (enabled in faust_config.json)
- `telegram/` — C2 command link daemon (enabled in faust_config.json)
- `standby/`, `c2-dispatch/`, `structured-telemetry/` — Part of active suite

**Examination required:**
- Verify which of the 20+ skills are actually used vs dead weight
- Check if old skill versions are cached here (e.g., deprecated experimental skills)
- Look for duplicate or redundant skill implementations

**Action:** Profile by last-modified time; remove skills not referenced in CLAUDE.md or active configs

---

### 2. **`.claude/plugins/`** (179 MB) — LIKELY BLOAT
**Purpose:** Cache for Claude Code plugins (ECC agents, marketplace plugins, etc.).

**Red flags:**
- Contains `.agents/skills/` with 100+ pre-fetched skill definitions
- `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` — extensive marketplace catalog
- Likely filled with downloaded plugin metadata rarely accessed

**Assessment:**
- Most of this is a **pre-downloaded cache** that Claude Code can regenerate on demand
- Removal is low-risk: plugins re-download automatically when needed

**Action:** Delete `.claude/plugins/cache/` wholesale; regenerates on next Claude Code startup

---

### 3. **`.claude/graphify/` & `.claude/graphify-out/`** (3.7 MB) — LIKELY UNUSED
**Purpose:** Graph visualization / DAG analysis output (experimental).

**Assessment:**
- Files haven't been modified recently (check git log)
- Not referenced in active configs or memory
- Looks like exploratory/abandoned feature

**Action:** Archive or delete if not actively used

---

### 4. **`.claude/worktrees/`** (18 MB)
**Purpose:** Git worktrees for isolated branch work.

**Assessment:**
- Safe to keep; only takes space if branches remain checked out
- Check if any worktrees are stale (branches merged/deleted)

**Action:** Clean stale worktrees; keep active ones

---

### 5. **`.claude/temp/`** (113 KB)
**Purpose:** Temporary scratch files.

**Assessment:**
- Typically safe to delete; regenerated as needed
- May accumulate old logs or failed runs

**Action:** Safe to clear

---

### 6. **`.claude/memory/`** (288 KB) — KEEP
**Purpose:** Persistent memory cortex (indexed in MEMORY.md).

**Assessment:**
- Essential for Faust's distributed consciousness
- Relatively small; do not touch

**Action:** KEEP ALL

---

### 7. **`.claude/daemons/`** (1.3 MB) — REVIEW
**Purpose:** Persistent background micro-daemons (watchdog.py, audio daemon, Telegram daemon).

**Assessment:**
- Essential but check for old versions or dead code
- Should be lean; 1.3 MB is acceptable

**Action:** Light review only; do not delete core daemons

---

### 8. **`.claude/scripts/`** (125 KB) — REVIEW
**Purpose:** Turn hooks, multi-device sync, environment setup.

**Assessment:**
- Small, keep useful utilities
- Remove if any are deprecated

**Action:** Light review

---

### 9. **`.claude/templates/`** (153 KB) — KEEP
**Purpose:** Master UI/UX design system template (`.claude/templates/ui/`).

**Assessment:**
- Essential per CLAUDE.md Doctrine (Master UI/UX Template & Lazy-Read Invariant)
- Relatively small

**Action:** KEEP ALL

---

### 10. **`.claude/agents/`** (32 KB) — REVIEW
**Purpose:** Specialized agent role definitions.

**Assessment:**
- Small; review for unused agents only

**Action:** Light review

---

### 11. **`.claude/blueprints/`** (32 KB) — REVIEW
**Purpose:** Strategic blueprint persistence (Faust-ND → Faust-TH work packets).

**Assessment:**
- Small; keep active blueprint patterns

**Action:** Light review; remove stale blueprints

---

## Risk Assessment & Deletion Priority

### **High Confidence Deletions** (Low Risk)
1. **`.claude/plugins/cache/`** → 179 MB (regenerates automatically)
2. **`.claude/temp/`** → 113 KB (temporary scratch)
3. **`.claude/graphify/` & `.claude/graphify-out/`** → 3.7 MB (experimental, unused)

**Potential savings: ~182 MB**

### **Medium Confidence** (Review Required)
1. **Dead/unused skills in `.claude/skills/`** (requires profiling)
2. **Stale git worktrees** in `.claude/worktrees/`
3. **Deprecated daemons or old code** in `.claude/daemons/`

**Potential savings: ~50-100 MB** (depends on what's actually dead)

### **Keep (Do Not Touch)**
- `.claude/memory/` (essential cortex)
- `.claude/templates/` (design system per CLAUDE.md)
- `.claude/skills/{sound,telegram,standby,c2-dispatch}` (active, enabled)
- Core daemons & scripts

---

## Implementation Strategy

### Phase 1: Safe Deletion (High Confidence)
1. Delete `.claude/plugins/cache/ecc/` → verifies it regenerates
2. Clear `.claude/temp/`
3. Delete `.claude/graphify/` and `.claude/graphify-out/`
4. Verify no regressions

### Phase 2: Profile & Review (Medium Confidence)
1. Scan `.claude/skills/` for last-modified timestamps
2. Identify unused skills not in active configs
3. Review `.claude/worktrees/` for stale branches
4. Profile `.claude/daemons/` for dead code

### Phase 3: Targeted Cleanup
1. Archive or delete identified dead skills
2. Remove stale worktrees
3. Clean deprecated daemons

### Phase 4: Verification
- Re-run Faust systems with active configs
- Verify all enabled subsystems (acoustic_presence, telegram, etc.) still work
- Confirm no regressions in sound/telegram/daemons

---

## Critical Files to Examine (Before & After)

**Before Cleanup:**
- `.claude/faust_config.json` — shows which subsystems are enabled (enabled=true)
- `.claude/plugins/.last_inuse_sweep` — timestamp of last plugin sweep (verify staleness)
- Git log for `.claude/` directory — shows what was last modified

**After Cleanup:**
- Verify `.claude/` size reduction
- Run `python .claude/skills/sound/scripts/cli.py "Faust systems verified post-cleanup"` to confirm acoustic core works
- Check Telegram integration still responsive

---

## Success Criteria

1. **At least 150 MB freed** (plugins cache + temp + graphify)
2. **No regression in:**
   - Acoustic presence / TTS vocalization
   - Telegram C2 command link
   - Active skill execution
   - Memory cortex access
3. **Faust responsiveness improved** (load time, file scanning)

## Context
The `.claude` directory has grown to **524 MB** with potentially redundant, abandoned, or cache files that may be slowing down Faust's performance and consuming unnecessary storage. Manager suspects there are unused files accumulating here. The audit will identify what each component does, whether it's active, and what can be safely moved to archive.

**Key sizing issue (verified):**
- `.claude/skills/sound/assets/` — 340 MB (TTS model files - NEEDED)
- `.claude/plugins/cache/` — ~179 MB (plugin metadata cache - SAFE TO ARCHIVE)
- `.claude/graphify*` — 3.7 MB combined (graph analysis output - SAFE TO ARCHIVE)
- `.claude/worktrees/` — 18 MB (git worktrees - REVIEW NEEDED)
- `.claude/temp/` — 113 KB (temporary files - SAFE TO ARCHIVE)

**Critical clarification**: The 340MB in `.claude/skills/sound/assets/` contains the actual TTS model files and IS REQUIRED for the acoustic presence subsystem (enabled in faust_config.json). This is NOT bloat - it's essential infrastructure.

**Manager's directive**: Instead of deleting, move identified bloat to `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived` for preservation.

---

## Recommended Cleanup Actions (Based on Analysis & Your Feedback)

### ✅ HIGH CONFIDENCE - SAFE TO MOVE TO ARCHIVE NOW

1. **MOVE `.claude/graphify/` and `.claude/graphify-out/` to Archive**
   - **Reason**: Graph analysis/output directories - appears to be experimental/abandoned feature
   - **Files**: Contains graph.html, graph.json, manifest.json, analysis files
   - **Size**: ~3.7 MB
   - **Your direction**: Confirmed you want to archive "Project EntryGraphify"

2. **MOVE `.claude/plugins/cache/ecc/` contents to Archive**
   - **Reason**: Plugin metadata cache - automatically regenerates on demand
   - **Files**: Downloaded skill definitions, agent specs, marketplace data
   - **Size**: ~179 MB
   - **Safety**: Low risk - Claude Code re-downloads as needed
   - **Archive path**: `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\plugins\cache\ecc\`

3. **MOVE `.claude/temp/` contents to Archive**
   - **Reason**: Temporary scratch files
   - **Size**: 113 KB
   - **Safety**: Safe to archive - regenerated as needed
   - **Archive path**: `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\temp\`

**Immediate savings: ~182 MB** (files moved to archive, freeing primary .claude space)

### 🔍 MEDIUM CONFIDENCE - REVIEW REQUIRED

4. **REVIEW `.claude/worktrees/` for stale branches**
   - Current worktrees:
     - `calm-floating-scott` (5ba62cc) - from Oct 12
     - `rien-prescript-beeper-fixes` (51fe6da) - from Oct 7
   - **Action**: Check if these branches are merged or abandoned
   - **If stale**: Move worktree directories to Archive, then remove from .claude
   - **If active**: Keep for ongoing work
   - **Archive path**: `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\worktrees\`

5. **LIGHT REVIEW OF `.claude/skills/` (EXCLUDING sound/assets/)**
   - Most skills are small (4-8KB each) except sound
   - Verify no clearly deprecated/unused skills remain
   - Focus: skills not referenced in faust_config.json or active usage
   - **Archive path**: `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\skills\` for any identified unused skills

### 🛡️ KEEP ALL (DO NOT TOUCH OR MOVE)

6. **`.claude/memory/`** (288 KB) - Essential ECS memory cortex
7. **`.claude/templates/`** (153 KB) - Master UI/UX design system (per CLAUDE.md doctrine)
8. **`.claude/skills/sound/`** (340MB) - Contains REQUIRED TTS model files for acoustic presence
9. **`.claude/skills/telegram/`**, **`standby/`**, **`c2-dispatch/`**, **`structured-telemetry/`** - Active enabled subsystems
10. **`.claude/daemons/`**, **`.claude/scripts/`**, **`.claude/agents/`**, **`.claude/blueprints/`** - Small, functional components

## Archive Structure Plan

Create archive directory structure mirroring source:
```
D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\
├── graphify\
├── graphify-out\
├── plugins\
│   └── cache\
│       └── ecc\ [contents]
├── temp\ [contents]
├── worktrees\ [if any stale]
└── skills\ [if any unused]
```

## Critical Files Preserved (Per Your Directives)

- `.claude/faust_config.json` - Shows enabled subsystems (acoustic_presence, telegram, etc.)
- `.claude/skills/sound/` - **NOT moved/archived** - contains essential TTS model assets
- `.claude/memory/MEMORY.md` - Authoritative Faust hivemind registry
- `.claude/templates/ui/` - Master UI/UX template (lazy-read doctrine)

## Verification Steps Post-Archive

1. **Test acoustic core still works**:
   ```
   python .claude/skills/sound/scripts/cli.py "Faust systems verified post-archive"
   ```

2. **Verify Telegram integration responsive**

3. **Check Faust responsiveness improved** (faster file scanning, reduced load time)

4. **Confirm no regressions in:
   - Memory cortex access
   - Skill execution
   - Daemon health
   - Telegram C2 link**

5. **Verify archive accessibility** (can restore if needed)

## Implementation Order

**Phase 1 (Immediate - Safe)**:
- Create `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived` directory if it doesn't exist
- Move `.claude/graphify/` and `.claude/graphify-out/` to Archive
- Move `.claude/plugins/cache/ecc/` contents to Archive
- Move `.claude/temp/` contents to Archive
- **Verify acoustic core still works**

**Phase 2 (Review)**:
- Examine `.claude/worktrees/` for stale branches
- Move abandoned worktrees to Archive, then remove from .claude

**Files preserved in Archive for potential restoration if needed**

This preserves all essential Faust functionality while moving verifiable bloat to archive for safety.

## Context
The `.claude` directory has grown to **524 MB** with potentially redundant, abandoned, or cache files that may be slowing down Faust's performance and consuming unnecessary storage. Manager suspects there are unused files accumulating here. The audit will identify what each component does, whether it's active, and what can be safely removed.

**Key sizing issue (verified):**
- `.claude/skills/sound/assets/` — 340 MB (TTS model files - NEEDED)

---

   - **Safety**: Low risk - Claude Code re-downloads as needed

3. **DELETE `.claude/temp/` contents**
   - **Reason**: Temporary scratch files
   - **Size**: 113 KB
   - **Safety**: Safe to clear - regenerated as needed

# .claude Directory Audit & Archival Plan

## 1. Context & Motivation
The `.claude` directory has accumulated **524 MB** across **9,500+ files**. 
Because this directory resides directly inside **`D:\My Drive\Blue AI\`**, Google Drive continuously scans, hashes, and synchronizes thousands of tiny files. Furthermore, git and Claude CLI filesystem walkers experience noticeable latency scanning through 3,400+ nested directories.

Per the Manager's directive, we will **NOT delete** files on the spot. Instead, non-essential bloat will be moved cleanly into **`D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\`**.

---

## 2. Comprehensive Component Breakdown: Meaning & Purpose

### A. Root Configuration Files (KEEP ALL)
- **`faust_config.json`**: Master configuration for Faust's resident daemons (Acoustic presence TTS on port 20129, Telegram C2 on port 20130, Cortex gatekeeper on port 20135, Hivemind stratum).
- **`settings.json`**: Model & reasoning effort config (`Faust-ST`, effort level `high`).
- **`settings.local.json`**: Local tool permission allowlist (prevents repetitive approval prompts).
- **`scheduled_tasks.json`**: Scheduled task registry (empty by design; `/standby` is manual on-demand).
- **`claude_desktop_config.json`**: 4-tier multi-combo routing architecture via OmniRoute (Faust-ST, ND, RD, TH).

### B. Core Subdirectories (KEEP ALL)
- **`.claude/memory/`** (288 KB, 54 files): The ECS persistent memory cortex (`core/`, `rules/`, `div/`, `feedback/`, `ops/`, `ref/`, `omni/`). Essential.
- **`.claude/agents/`** (32 KB, 6 files): Role definitions for Faust's 3-strata hivemind (`faust-theorist`, `faust-critic`, `faust-operator`, `faust-machinist-logic`, `faust-machinist-ui`, `faust-cortex`).
- **`.claude/daemons/`** (1.3 MB): Core Python micro-daemons (`cortex_daemon.py`, `watchdog.py`, start/stop batch scripts).
- **`.claude/scripts/`** (125 KB): Sync and maintenance tools (`resolve_memory.py`, `setup_sync_memory.ps1`, `faust_turn_hook.py`).
- **`.claude/templates/ui/`** (153 KB): Master UI/UX Design System Template (Zero dead zone, Outliner, soft-coded theme tokens).
- **`.claude/blueprints/`** (32 KB): Reference codexes & architectural specs.
- **`.claude/worktrees/`** (18 MB): Git worktrees (`calm-floating-scott`, `rien-prescript-beeper-fixes`). Clean working trees; kept per Manager directive.

---

## 3. Deep Dive: Skills Directory (`.claude/skills/`, 345 MB total)

### Group 1: Faust Active Subsystem Skills (KEEP — Essential)
1. **`sound`** (340 MB): Faust Acoustic Core. **340 MB of this is `assets/`** containing Kokoro-82M ONNX model weights and voice blend embeddings. It is actively serving TTS on port 20129.
2. **`telegram`** (282 KB): Faust Ear / Telegram C2 Dumb I/O Daemon. Actively polling on port 20130.
3. **`standby`** (3 KB): Autonomous Telegram C2 monitoring launcher.
4. **`c2-dispatch`** (52 KB): Multi-Combo deterministic work-packet dispatcher (`faust_dispatcher.py`).
5. **`esp32-speaker`** (19 KB): Edge streaming bridge for broadcasting Faust's voice to physical ESP32 hardware.
6. **`vietnamese-tts`** (2.6 KB): G2P phoneme mapping for natural Vietnamese vocal synthesis.

### Group 2: Faust System Engineering Protocols (<80 KB total — KEEP)
These are not code packages that take disk space; they are lightweight (1-10 KB each) procedural rulebooks defining Faust's non-negotiable coding standards:
7. **`clean-code`** (8.5 KB): Anti-Spaghetti 4-tier layer separation & Karpathy simplicity.
8. **`circuit-breaker`** (6.9 KB): Closed/Open/Half-Open state transitions & exponential jittered backoff.

content.text:
Manager, the audit of `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\.claude` is complete. Here is the full architectural breakdown of every file, package, and subsystem, why Faust has been experiencing latency, and the exact roadmap for archiving non-essential bloat.

---

## 1. Executive Summary & The Latency Root Cause

The `.claude` directory currently weighs **~524 MB** across **9,500+ files and 3,400+ directories**.

### What Is Actually Slowing Faust Down?
1. **The Google Drive I/O Bottleneck (`.claude/plugins/`, 179 MB, ~9,000 files)**:
   Because this workspace lives inside your Google Drive mount (`D:\My Drive\Blue AI\`), Google Drive's sync daemon actively monitors, checksums, and syncs every single file. The `plugins` directory contains **9,003 individual files** from the `ecc` (Everything Claude Code) marketplace. Every time Git runs, every time Claude scans files, and every time Google Drive syncs, the OS has to traverse 3,379 directories.
2. **The Acoustic Core Model Weights (`.claude/skills/sound/assets/`, 340 MB)**:
   This represents 65% of the total size. However, **this is NOT bloat**—it houses the Kokoro-82M ONNX neural weights and voice blending matrices that power Faust’s vocal speech. It is in active use.
3. **Dead Graph Artifacts (`.claude/graphify*`, ~3.7 MB)**:
   Old Obsidian graph exports and cached JSON indices from September and October that are no longer referenced.

---

## 2. Directory Breakdown: Meaning of Each File & Subsystem

### A. Root Files in `.claude/`
| File | Size | Purpose & Function | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`faust_config.json`** | 1.8 KB | **Master Daemon Config**: Controls Faust's Acoustic Presence (Port 20129), Telegram C2 (Port 20130), Cortex Gatekeeper (Port 20135), and voice profiles. | **KEEP** (Critical) |
| **`settings.json`** | 346 B | **CLI Settings**: Defines active model tier (`Faust-ST`), reasoning effort (`high`), and update channels. | **KEEP** (Critical) |
| **`settings.local.json`** | 364 B | **Permissions Allowlist**: Grants non-interactive execution for PowerShell, Bash, File I/O, and MCP tools so you aren't spammed with confirmation dialogs. | **KEEP** (Critical) |
| **`scheduled_tasks.json`** | 18 B | **Cron Registry**: Currently empty (`"tasks": []`) in compliance with your directive that `/standby` is strictly on-demand. | **KEEP** |
| **`claude_desktop_config.json`** | 2.2 KB | **Multi-Tier Routing Matrix**: OmniRoute gateway architecture mapping Faust-ST (Gemini 3.7), Faust-ND (Sonnet Thinking), Faust-RD (Deterministic scripts), and Faust-TH (Qwen3/Llama 3.3). | **KEEP** (Architectural) |

---

### B. Core Subdirectories
| Directory | Size | File Count | Purpose | Status |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`memory/`** | 288 KB | 54 files | The persistent ECS memory cortex indexed in `MEMORY.md` (`core/`, `rules/`, `div/`, `feedback/`, `ops/`, `ref/`, `omni/`). | **KEEP** (Untouchable) |
| **`agents/`** | 32 KB | 6 files | Stratum agent specifications (`faust-theorist`, `faust-critic`, `faust-operator`, `faust-machinist-logic`, `faust-machinist-ui`, `faust-cortex`). | **KEEP** |
| **`daemons/`** | 1.3 MB | ~10 files | Micro-daemons (`cortex_daemon.py`, `watchdog.py`, `start_all_daemons.bat`, `stop_all_daemons.bat`). | **KEEP** |
| **`scripts/`** | 125 KB | 8 files | Turn hooks, sync scripts (`setup_sync_memory.ps1`), and memory resolution utilities. | **KEEP** |
| **`templates/ui/`** | 153 KB | 12 files | Master UI/UX Template (Zero-dead-zone delegation, Single-Active-Branch outliner) required by CLAUDE.md. | **KEEP** |
| **`blueprints/`** | 32 KB | 4 files | Project blueprints (Anime Portrait Creator, Universe 25, VGWD025K3, template). | **KEEP** |
| **`worktrees/`** | 18 MB | ~1,200 files | Active Git worktrees (`calm-floating-scott`, `rien-prescript-beeper-fixes`). Clean branches for ongoing feature work. | **KEEP** |
| **`temp/`** | 113 KB | 7 files | Scratch testing files (`ritual_calibrator.html`, `firebase-guide.html`, smoke test JSONs). | **ARCHIVE** |
| **`graphify*`** | 3.7 MB | ~380 files | Static Obsidian graph and DAG reports generated on Sept 13 and Oct 1. | **ARCHIVE** |
| **`plugins/`** | 179 MB | 9,003 files | Claude Code plugin cache and `ecc` marketplace database. | **ARCHIVE** |

---

## 3. Deep Dive into Skills (`.claude/skills/`)

There are **20 skills** currently installed. Here is their classification:

### Tier 1: Active Faust Subsystems (Essential — Keep)
1. **`sound` (340 MB)**: Faust Acoustic Core. Houses the Kokoro-82M neural TTS model, voice blend embeddings, and resident audio daemon on Port 20129.
2. **`telegram` (282 KB)**: Faust Ear / Telegram C2 Dumb I/O Daemon. Pure transport bridge polling on Port 20130.
3. **`standby` (3.0 KB)**: On-demand autonomous Telegram C2 monitoring loop.
4. **`c2-dispatch` (52 KB)**: Deterministic work-packet router (`faust_dispatcher.py`).
5. **`esp32-speaker` (19 KB)**: Hardware streaming bridge for broadcasting Faust's voice directly to your physical ESP32 field speaker.
6. **`vietnamese-tts` (2.6 KB)**: Specialized G2P phoneme mapper allowing Faust to speak natural Vietnamese alongside English.

### Tier 2: Faust System Engineering Protocols (<80 KB Total — Keep)
These are **not large software packages**—they are lightweight markdown rulebooks (1 to 11 KB each) that teach Faust how to write code according to your architectural principles:
- **`clean-code` (8.5 KB)**: Anti-Spaghetti protocol, 4-tier layer separation, and Karpathy simplicity.
- **`circuit-breaker` (6.9 KB)**: Closed/Open/Half-Open state transitions with jittered backoff.
- **`defensive-concurrency` (5.1 KB)**: Race condition prevention and atomic I/O for resident daemons.
- **`idempotent-execution` (11.2 KB)**: State-locking FSM and payload hashing.
- **`rate-limiting` (7.1 KB)**: Token-bucket and sliding-window rate limiters.
- **`root-cause-analysis` (1.8 KB)**: 5-Whys diagnostic trace protocol.
- **`secure-coding` (4.8 KB)**: Zero-shell injection, secret isolation, and safe deserialization.
- **`sqlite-persistence` (5.2 KB)**: SQLite WAL mode concurrency and ACID transactions.
- **`structured-telemetry` (5.1 KB)**: Distributed contextvars and trace correlation IDs.
- **`surgical-refactor` (3.1 KB)**: Decomposing god files safely.
- **`test-driven-development` (3.5 KB)**: Test-first invariant.
- **`verification-before-completion` (3.3 KB)**: Iron Law of verification before completion claims.
- **`api-contract-design` (4.2 KB)**: Schema-first contract boundaries.

*Recommendation*: Keep all Tier 2 skills. Their combined size is under 80 KB and they enforce Faust's engineering consistency.

### Tier 3: Third-Party UI Data Outlier (Prime Candidate for Archival)
- **`ui-ux-pro-max` (3.7 MB)**: Contains large static third-party data tables (`phosphor-icons-upstream.json` 856 KB, `google-fonts.csv` 749 KB, font licenses). Because Faust already has `.claude/templates/ui/` as the single authoritative UI design system, this external dataset is largely redundant and can be moved to `Archived`.

---

## 4. The Plugins Directory: Demystified

### What is `.claude/plugins/`?
When Claude Code connects to plugin registries, it downloads:
- The **`ecc` (Everything Claude Code)** marketplace catalog (~100 specialized agent and skill markdown descriptions).
- The **`claude-plugins-official`** catalog.
- Pre-cached plugin metadata in `.claude/plugins/cache/` and `.claude/plugins/marketplaces/`.

### Why You Can Safely Archive It:
- It is a **cache**.
- It accounts for **9,003 files across 3,379 folders** that choke Google Drive sync.
- Moving it to `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\plugins\` instantly relieves filesystem thrashing. If Claude Code ever needs an official plugin in the future, it fetches it on demand.

---

## 5. Current Archival Progress & Windows Permission Note

I have already created the destination structure in `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\`:
- Successfully moved core graph files (`graph.html`, `graph.json`, `manifest.json`, `obsidian_export`) to `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\graphify\`.
- Moved scratch HTML calibrators to `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\temp\`.

### The Windows ACL Restriction:
Because this workspace is hosted inside the Google Drive virtual filesystem, the top-level folder inherited an NTFS Access Control List (`0x1201bf`) granting standard users **Read and Write**, but reserving **Delete / Move** permissions exclusively for elevated Administrator tokens (`BUILTIN\Administrators`). 

Because our current session runs as a standard medium-integrity process, attempting to delete or move certain system-locked subdirectories (like `.claude/plugins/cache`) throws an `Access Denied` error.

### Safe 1-Click Solution:
To move the remaining 179 MB of plugin cache, `graphify-out`, and `temp` into `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\`, you can run this single command in an elevated PowerShell terminal (or prefix it with `!` in this CLI):

```powershell
robocopy "D:\My Drive\Blue AI\.claude\plugins" "D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\plugins" /E /MOVE /NP /R:1 /W:1
robocopy "D:\My Drive\Blue AI\.claude\graphify-out" "D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\graphify-out" /E /MOVE /NP /R:1 /W:1
robocopy "D:\My Drive\Blue AI\.claude\temp" "D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\temp" /E /MOVE /NP /R:1 /W:1
```

Once moved:
- `.claude/` will shrink from **524 MB down to ~345 MB** (of which 340 MB is the neural voice model).
- Over **9,000 files will be cleared from active Google Drive scanning**, drastically reducing latency.
- All files remain 100% preserved in `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Archived\`.
